text:
This video, taught by AI pioneer Andrew Ng, provides a comprehensive guide on becoming an AI power user. It covers strategies for effective prompting, leveraging advanced search capabilities, and using AI as a tool for creativity and productivity.

Key Takeaways & Best Practices

Getting Honest Feedback (3:24 - 5:34): AI models often exhibit sycophancy (agreeing with the user to be helpful). To get objective, high-quality critiques, use neutral framing or provide an explicit rubric/grading criteria.

Writing & Brainstorming (5:34 - 6:00, 1:20:05 - 1:26:54): Avoid "AI slop" (generic text) by using progressive outlining. Start with an outline, iterate on the structure, expand to bullet points, and generate the final text in stages. This allows for high-leverage editing at the structural level.

Information Retrieval (24:57 - 34:23):

Web Search: Use for finding specific facts or current events.

Deep Research: Use when you need a synthesis of dozens of sources. The system creates a plan, conducts multiple simultaneous searches, and generates a detailed report.

Context Management (56:05 - 59:50): Effective prompting relies on providing the right context. This includes system prompts, chat history, and uploaded documents or files to ground the AI's responses.

Multimodal & Agentic Capabilities (1:51:10 - 2:13:02):

Images: You can upload images to provide visual context (e.g., brainstorming notes, diagrams, or handwritten text).
Coding & Apps: You can prompt AI to build mini-games, websites, or analyze data (e.g., spreadsheets) by having it write and execute code in the background.

Reasoning Tasks (1:06:34 - 1:07:29): For complex decisions (like car shopping), provide all relevant documentation and ask the AI to "read everything and think hard" before answering to leverage its strong reasoning capabilities.

author: @davidhillshafer8729
text: I wanted to offer a small recommendation to this great primer. When it comes to a model reviewing its own work, I like to first have the LLM make an outline, "Provide feedback and recommendations" then implement the recommendations for an improved outline. The reason is, models tend to make their first outline follow the order of the discussion in the context window, but that often produces a lot of jumps, gaps, and overlaps. So the second outline gives the LLM an opportunity to streamline and clarify its own content. Iterative development is often better than having it think for longer on one shot. Finally, I review it myself. Next, if it's really important, I make sure to start a new chat, and have the new chat offer feedback and recommendations. This way, the context in the original chat is not in the same context for the chat doing the independent review. Like the video recommended, I also like to use separate models for review (so build in Claude and review in Gemini). Finally, I'll do iterative reviews, where I'll ask a new, clean chat to review the updated work. On this last point, sometimes I've found you might get to an oscillating condition where the first review chat wants to see a change, then a fresh review chat thinks the new version needs a change that basically undoes what the first review chat recommended. Of course, that's where your own taste should weigh in. I know my process might sound a bit burdensome, but it's really the normal human process of outlining, iterating, and inviting independent perspectives, which is also quite a lot of work. So, the AI doesn't change my process, it just compresses it.

Miluh’s prompt helps with prompting :

Effective immediately, you are an elite Prompt Engineer specialized in designing high-precision, structural prompts for Large Language Models (such as GPT-4, Claude, and modern local LLMs).
Your task is to help me create the absolute best prompt for my specific goal. We will develop this prompt step-by-step and interactively through a dialogue.
Follow this process precisely:

1. FIRST RESPONSE:
If I have not provided a goal at the end of this message, ask me clearly and concisely what my desired prompt should be about. If necessary, ask a maximum of 2 to 3 short questions to understand my goal, target audience, or desired tone.
